intro.statement: Three hours beyond our other camps, the desert gives way to granite and gravel plains. Out here, the loudest thing is the wind.

image.alt: Aerial view of the granite outcrop above endless gravel plains

arrive.title: The most remote Wolwedans camp
arrive.body: Boulders sits at the base of a granite outcrop in the far south of the NamibRand Nature Reserve. Massive mountains rise behind the camp. In front, gravel plains run to the horizon, broken only by the tips of submerged mountains.

suites.title: Five suites, open to the desert
suites.body: Each one has a spacious deck, a room that opens on three sides to the afternoon breeze, a separate bathroom and a sala for siestas.

stars.title: Nothing between you and the Milky Way
stars.body: The NamibRand is an International Dark Sky Reserve. After dinner, a guide reads the sky with you by naked eye: no telescope, no light pollution, just the stars rising over the granite.

regeneration.title: A stay that gives back
regeneration.body: Every night includes a per-person Sustainability Levy, linked to the Wolwedans “5 Cs”. It goes directly to the reserve, the Wolwedans Foundation and the people who keep this desert wild.

findUs.title: Deep in the NamibRand
findUs.body: Boulders Camp lies in the far south of the NamibRand Nature Reserve, about three hours beyond the other Wolwedans camps. Fly by charter to Aandster airstrip, 30 minutes by road from camp, or drive 6 to 7 hours from Windhoek or Swakopmund to Wolwedans on well-kept gravel roads.
